question: A plane electromagnetic wave is represented by $E_x = 120\sin(kz - \omega t)\text{ V m}^{-1}$. It travels in vacuum. Determine the amplitude of the magnetic field and write the corresponding expression for the magnetic field if it is directed along the $y$-axis.

options.A: $B_0=\dfrac{E_0}{c}=4.0\times10^{-7}\text{ T}$. Since the wave travels along $+z$ and $\vec{E}$ is along $+x$, $\vec{B}$ must be along $-y$. Hence $B_y=-4.0\times10^{-7}\sin(kz-\omega t)\text{ T}$.
options.B: $B_0=\dfrac{c}{E_0}=2.5\times10^6\text{ T}$. The magnetic field is $B_y=2.5\times10^6\sin(kz-\omega t)\text{ T}$.
options.C: $B_0=4.0\times10^{-7}\text{ T}$. The magnetic field is $B_y=4.0\times10^{-7}\cos(kz-\omega t)\text{ T}$, because electric and magnetic fields are $90^\circ$ out of phase.
options.D:
$B_0=\dfrac{E_0}{c}=\dfrac{120}{3.0\times10^8}=4.0\times10^{-7}\text{ T}$.
For propagation along $+z$, with $\vec{E}$ along $+x$, $\vec{B}$ must be along $+y$ so that $\vec{E}\times\vec{B}$ is along $+z$.
Thus $B_y=4.0\times10^{-7}\sin(kz-\omega t)\text{ T}$.
